by: gazette session 4, step 5.3 (proposed; the integrator appends it)
title: An overseas company leaving New Zealand: its intention to cease to carry on business here, or its application for removal from the overseas register (Gazette section cb)

landmarks: the Gazette's own section code cb in the notice number (<year>-cb<n>): every notice so filed, and no other

signals_note: Recognised by the Gazette's classification, never by title words: the title is the company's name.
notes: Two shapes. notice: one overseas company, its name the title less the brackets that are not the name's own ('(New Zealand branch)', '(the "overseas company")', '(formerly …)', '(ACN …)'); the action from the notice's head: ceasing to carry on business in New Zealand (Companies Act 1993 s 343), or an application for removal from the overseas register; the 'Company No.' where the text prints exactly one; the day it ceases where printed; 'Dated'. list: the Registrar's 'Notice of Intention to Remove Overseas Companies From the Register', cut as the removal profile cuts its lists. No address is read.
applies_to: 2,607 notices, 2000 to 2026 (measured 20 October 2026: 2,601 read, 2,885 company rows, 95.4% held by the companies register)
process: Read the company from the title (or the list).
Read the action, section, number, the day it ceases and the Dated day.
gates: Every cb notice gives a company or is a catch-log line.
A title that is not a company's name, or a notice with no action the reader knows, is a catch-log line, never a guess.
on_fail: set aside the part or the notice; publish the rest

by: gazette session 4, step 5.3 (proposed; the integrator appends it)
title: The Registrar's notice of intention to restore companies or limited partnerships to the register (Gazette section ot)

landmarks: the Gazette's own section code ot in the notice number (<year>-ot<n>)
and 'restore' or 'restoration' in the title, or 'propose(s) to restore' or 'intend to restore' in the opening words

signals_note: Section ot ('companies: other') also holds prohibitions, amalgamations and the Registrar's rectifications; only the restorations are this profile. A restoration under ds stays with the removal profile.
notes: One shape: a list, one company or many, each followed by 'Applicant:' and the applicant's name and address. The applicant is often a person and the address often a home, so neither is read: each company is the text before an 'Applicant:', less everything up to the last comma that is not inside a name ('Able Company, Limited') and the address's closing town or postcode; the first is the longest end of the opening words after a stop that is a name and no prose. A number after the name is taken, behind the old registry office's two letters where printed ('AK. 123456'). The day objections close; 'Dated'; a court order restoring is said so.
applies_to: 888 notices, 2000 to 2026 (measured 20 October 2026: 868 read, 31,515 company rows, 93.1% held by the companies register; 166 rows a catch-log line)
process: Find the list by its 'Applicant:' markers.
Cut each company from the text before its applicant; never read the applicant.
Read the section, the objection day and the Dated day.
gates: Every ot notice titled a restoration gives a company or is a catch-log line.
A row that does not end in a legal suffix is a catch-log line, never a guess.
No applicant's name or address is held anywhere.
on_fail: set aside the part or the notice; publish the rest

by: gazette session 4, step 5.3 (proposed; the integrator appends it)
title: Incorporated societies and charitable trust boards dissolved, their dissolution revoked, or to be removed or restored (Gazette sections is and ct)

landmarks: the Gazette's own section code is or ct in the notice number

and a title of dissolution, revocation, intention to remove, restore or dissolve, or removal of societies or trusts; never a direction for the disposition of surplus assets, a scheme, a variation or financial statements

signals_note: Sections is and ct also hold directions on a dissolved body's surplus assets and applications to approve or vary charitable schemes; only the titles above are this profile.
notes: One shape: the Registrar's list. An opening sentence (ending at a colon, else at a stop after prose or the Act's year), then each body's name and its registration number, a revocation printing the day of the dissolution it undoes after the number '(3 May 2004)', the older lists 'Date of Dissolution: <day>' before the name; up to 'Dated', 'With this publication' or the Registrar's signature. A list that prints no numbers is cut at each bracketed day. The old registry office's letters after a name ('AK. I.S.', 'C.T.', 'WN') are dropped. A row that reads as prose is a catch-log line. The action: dissolution, revocation of dissolution, intention to dissolve (including a body's own request), intention to restore. The number is looked up in the societies' and trust boards' registers, never the companies'. No address is printed or read.
applies_to: 1,813 notices, 2000 to 2026 (measured 20 October 2026: 1,697 read, 33,749 body rows, 98.7% held by the register, 27,707 of 30,714 printed numbers agreeing by name)
process: Cut each body at its number (or its bracketed day).
Read the action, section, each body's dissolution day where printed, and the Dated day.
gates: Every is or ct notice titled as above gives a body or is a catch-log line.
A row that reads as prose is a catch-log line, never a guess.
on_fail: set aside the part or the notice; publish the rest
